chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn 'Atiyyah, from Abi Hamzah al-Thumali, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, it is not that one year rains more than another, but He (Allah) places it where He wills. Indeed, when a people commit sins, Allah turns away from them the rain He had destined for them in that year and sends it to other lands, seas, and mountains. And indeed, Allah puns the ants in their holes, withholding rain from the earth because of the sins of those present there, although He has made a way and path for it to reach the place of those who obey. Then Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Take heed, O people of insight and intellect.

Then he said: We found in the book of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: When adultery becomes prevalent, sudden death increases. When measures are cheated, Allah seizes them with drought and deficiency. When Zakat is withheld, the earth withholds its blessings from crops, fruits, and minerals. When they are unjust in judgments and cooperate in oppression and aggression, and when they break their covenants, Allah sends their enemies against them. When they sever ties of kinship, wealth falls into the hands of their evil ones. When they do not enjoin good nor forbid evil, and do not follow the virtuous from my Ahl al-Bayt, Allah will make their evil ones have authority over them; so their virtuous ones will call out (pray), but their call will not be answered.
ai.seo_question: What are the divine consequences of specific sins like adultery and withholding Zakat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq narrates this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS), who clarifies that rainfall variations are not random but are divinely redirected based on communal sins, a concept rooted in the principle of 'Tasrif' (divine redirection of blessings). The text further links specific transgressions like withholding Zakat and injustice to tangible earthly consequences, culminating in the rejection of the righteous's prayers, a theme echoed in the sayings of Amir al-Mu'minin found in the hadith.
